content.overview: BNS s. 245 — Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due. BNS restatement of IPC 209. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 209. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 245 is the rule on “Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due”. The section provides that whoever fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be passed against him at the suit of any person for a sum not due or for a larger sum than is due to such person or for any property or interest in property to which such person is not entitled, or fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be executed against him after it has been satisfied, or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 245 exists so that “Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.

The provision in detail
245. Whoever fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be passed against him at the suit of any person for a sum not due or for a larger sum than is due to such person or for any property or interest in property to which such person is not entitled, or fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be executed against him after it has been satisfied, or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be passed against him at the suit of any person for a sum not due or for a larger sum than is due to such person or for any property or interest in property to which such person is not entitled, or fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be executed against him after it has been satisfied, or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A institutes a suit against Z. Z, knowing that A is likely to obtain a decree against him, fraudulently suffers a judgment to pass against him for a larger amount at the suit of B, who has no just claim against him, in order that B, either on his own account or for the benefit of Z, may share in the proceeds of any sale of Z’s property which may be made under A’s decree. Z has committed an offence under this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 245 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.
